::: {.home-intro}
::: {.home-intro-copy}
Hi, I’m Rey Joseph “RJ” Nieto.

I am a mathematician, university instructor, and columnist for the *Manila
Bulletin*. I am studying for an MSc in Science, Technology, Engineering and
Public Policy at [University College London (UCL)](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/). I
hold a First Class Honours BSc in Mathematics from the [University of
Bristol](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/) and [teach mathematics and information
technology](teaching/index.qmd) at [Bulacan State University
(BulSU)](https://bulsu.edu.ph/) in the Philippines.

Alongside my teaching, I am studying dynamical systems, functional analysis,
and measure theory and probability. These subjects support my [continuing
research in topology-informed computer vision](research/index.qmd), where I am
examining the reliability of measurements derived from retinal images and
possible applications in biomedical and industrial imaging.

Before returning to mathematics, I worked in journalism, broadcasting, public
affairs, technical writing, and government communications. My current column,
[*Calculated*](calculated/index.qmd), marks my return to public commentary.
:::

## Research

My final-year project began as a topology-informed classifier for diabetic
retinopathy. During testing, however, a simulated rotation of roughly three
degrees drove it close to chance performance. That failure became the
interesting part: I began asking whether the different ways mathematical
measurements respond to blur, rotation, resolution changes, and sensor noise
could reveal what had happened to an image.

I am now examining how sampling and interpolation on a pixel grid affect those
measurements, and whether topological and geometric measurements leave
different signatures when an image degrades. This remains ongoing research.

[Current research](research/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
